classification.difficultyReason: Find and validate two possible angles, sketch both triangles, and use each case to calculate a side.

content.prompt: Consider $\triangle PQR$ in which $p=7\text{ cm}$, $q=15\text{ cm}$ and $\angle P=25^{\circ}50'$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the two possible sizes of $\angle Q$ to the nearest minute, then sketch the two triangles.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin Q}{15}&=\frac{\sin(25^{\circ}50')}{7}\\\sin Q&=\frac{15\sin(25^{\circ}50')}{7}\\Q_1&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{15\sin(25^{\circ}50')}{7}\right)\\Q_1&\approx69.028778^{\circ}\\Q_2&=180^{\circ}-Q_1\\Q_2&\approx110.971222^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
The larger possibility satisfies $110.971222^{\circ}+25^{\circ}50'<180^{\circ}$, so both triangles are valid.

Thus $Q=69^{\circ}02'$ or $110^{\circ}58'$ to the nearest minute.

spec.mathematics: PR=15 cm, QR=7 cm, P=25°50′, Q≈69°02′. Coordinates are derived from the givens and unrounded sine-rule solution.

spec.mathematics: PR=15 cm, QR=7 cm, P=25°50′, Q≈110°58′. Coordinates are derived from the givens and unrounded sine-rule solution.

children.label: b
children.prompt: For each possible size of $\angle Q$, find side length $r$ in cm, correct to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded values of $Q$ from part a.

For the acute value of $Q$:
$$\begin{align*}R_1&=180^{\circ}-25^{\circ}50'-Q_1\\R_1&\approx85.137889^{\circ}\\\frac{r_1}{\sin R_1}&=\frac{7}{\sin(25^{\circ}50')}\\r_1&=\frac{7\sin R_1}{\sin(25^{\circ}50')}\\r_1&\approx16.0\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
For the obtuse value of $Q$:
$$\begin{align*}R_2&=180^{\circ}-25^{\circ}50'-Q_2\\R_2&\approx43.195445^{\circ}\\\frac{r_2}{\sin R_2}&=\frac{7}{\sin(25^{\circ}50')}\\r_2&=\frac{7\sin R_2}{\sin(25^{\circ}50')}\\r_2&\approx11.0\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
